name: Borth coastal defence reef (Phase 1, Ceredigion, Wales)
status: DERIVED: every number in "global", "lines" and "extra_layers" is computed by the script from the published 3D-model data (no new measurement); the model inputs and their sources are in "key_inputs" and in the model METHODS_3D.md.

version.name: Laser survey edge (Welsh Government LiDAR, 19 Mar 2022)

frame: x alongshore (+ toward SOUTH, bearing 179.57 deg T); y offshore (+ toward WEST, bearing 269.57 deg T); origin = foot of the perpendicular from the centroid of both mounds on the defence line
datum: z = metres above MSL; MSL = +0.31 mODN (+-0.15, estimate); z_MSL = z_ODN - 0.31 (model.js datum.equation)
shoreline_definition: y = 0 is the DEFENCE LINE (back of the shingle beach, z about +4.9 m MSL), NOT the MSL waterline. The MSL waterline is where the modelled natural seabed crosses z = 0 (computed per line, key y_msl_crossing_m).
units: metres; offshore_m = model y (distance from the model shoreline y = 0, positive offshore); elevations in metres above MSL (z up); x = alongshore model axis

method.reef_surface: model.js versions[lidar_2022].grid.h_cm_b64 (int16 cm, z_MSL, 1 m cells, rows = y, cols = x): 1 m LiDAR DSM (Welsh Government, flown 19 Mar 2022, lightly smoothed) inside the exposed-rock outline, plus the Royal Haskoning toe berm / blanket slopes (drawings 9V5090/1021-1023) down to the modelled seabed. Zones: 1 armour, 2 toe berm, 3 blanket/apron.
method.seabed: model.js seabed (5 m grid, z_MSL): thin-plate/RBF fit to the Royal Haskoning drawing nodes + Fig. 2 contours (build_3d.py seabed_grid).

sampling.interpolation: seabed: bilinear on the model grid / analytic profile; reef surface: NaN-aware (normalised) bilinear on the reef grid; profiles at constant model x
sampling.footprint_rule: a reef cell belongs to the footprint if (reef surface - natural seabed) >= 0.10 m (ASSUMPTION, avoids zero-thickness tapers)
sampling.crest_line: x of the shallowest reef-surface cell
sampling.crest_zone: contiguous points on the line within 0.10 m of the line maximum (ASSUMPTION)
sampling.ramp: seaward ramp = from the seaward edge of the crest zone to the seaward end of the reef run (the toe); ramp_length = horizontal distance, ramp_rise = reef-surface drop over it, mean_seaward_slope = rise/length
sampling.max_seaward_slope: maximum over the ramp of (z[y-1 m] - z[y+1 m]) / 2 m (central difference, 2 m baseline), tan, degrees and 1:n
sampling.toe: seaward toe = most offshore point of the reef run (reef surface still >= 0.10 m above the seabed); the reef elevation, seabed elevation and thickness there are reported (thickness > 0.5 m means the model surface is cut at its outline, not at the seabed)
sampling.gap_bridging: gaps up to 12 m along a line are bridged when forming the reef run (ASSUMPTION; only Narrowneck is affected)
sampling.alongshore_length: span = x_max - x_min of footprint cells with reef surface >= level; union = number of x-columns containing such a cell * dx. Two levels are reported because "crest -0.5 m" is ambiguous: (a) z >= -0.5 m MSL and (b) z >= crest - 0.5 m
sampling.offshore_distance: offshore_m is measured from the model shoreline y = 0 (definition in shoreline_definition); offshore_from_msl_line_m uses the first downward crossing of z = 0 (MSL) of the modelled natural seabed on the same line

key_inputs.input: reef surface (exposed rock, LiDAR DSM) and water edge

sources.lidar2022: Welsh Government (2022). *LiDAR 2020-22, 1 m DSM and DTM, tile SN6089*, flown 2022-03-19 03:15-03:20 UTC. DataMapWales; Open Government Licence. https://dmwproductionblob.blob.core.windows.net/lidar-zips/2020-22/dsm/wg_del_29_260289_20220319dsm.tif (DTM: same path with dtm), accessed 2026-10-06 (registry img-24)

key_inputs.input: toe berm / blanket / armour design (crest +0.50/+1.00/+1.50 mODN, slopes 1:3-1:5, berm 1.35 m 1:1.5)

sources.drg1020-1023: Haskoning UK Ltd for Ceredigion County Council (2010-11). *Borth Coastal Protection Scheme - Phase 1*, drawings 9V5090/1020, /1021, /1022, /1023 rev C1 (For Construction, Jan 2011). http://www.borthcommunity.info/index.php/planning-drawings/65-planning-drawings, accessed 2026-10-06 (registry img-20..23)

key_inputs.input: seabed contours around the reefs (Fig. 2) and offshore gradient

sources.hrpp576f2: Rigden, T., Stewart, T., Allsop, W. and Johnson, A. (2013). *Surf reefs - physical modelling results, not pipe dreams*. HR Wallingford report HRPP576; ICE Coasts, Marine Structures and Breakwaters, Edinburgh, Sept 2013, Fig 2. https://eprints.hrwallingford.com/931/1/HRPP576_SurfReefs.pdf, accessed 2026-10-06 (registry img-17)
sources.emodnet: EMODnet Bathymetry Consortium (2024). *EMODnet Digital Bathymetry (DTM 2024)*. https://doi.org/10.12770/cf51df64-56f9-4a99-b1aa-36b8d7b743a1 (CC BY 4.0); survey cells CDI 115084 (OceanWise Ltd), accessed 2026-10-06 (registry img-14..16)

key_inputs.input: datum / tide levels (MSL = +0.31 mODN estimate; LAT = -2.44 mODN)

sources.ref3: Royal HaskoningDHV (2011). *West of Wales Shoreline Management Plan 2*, Section 4 Coastal Area C Introduction, p. 4C.3, water-level table (Aberystwyth). https://www.grwparfordirolgorllewincymru.cymru/sites/default/files/2019-06/4c1%20-%20Section%204%20Coastal%20Area%20C%20Introduction.pdf, accessed 2026-10-06
sources.ref4: National Tidal and Sea Level Facility (n.d.). *Chart datum and ordnance datum: differences at selected ports*. https://ntslf.org/tides/datum, accessed 2026-10-06

caveats: The 1 m LiDAR DSM sees block tops, about 0.1-0.3 m above the design surface (model.js versions[0].note).
The default 3D confidence is MEDIUM; bed under the reef is interpolated from design drawings, Fig. 2 contours and checked against Navionics (datum +-0.6 m).

The model has TWO structures: northern boot-shaped surf reef (crest +0.50 mODN) and southern oval shore-parallel breakwater (crest +1.50 mODN) which is NOT a surf reef. Reef metrics below are for the whole footprint incl. both unless a mask is given; the surf reef is the northern one (x < 0).

centreline.definition: cross-shore line (constant model x) at the alongshore mid-point of the reef footprint bounding box

crest_line.definition: cross-shore line (constant model x) through the shallowest crest cell of the reef surface (ties within 0.02 m: the cell nearest the middle of the shallowest plateau)

second_crest_line.definition: cross-shore line through the shallowest reef cell on the OTHER side of the centreline than the main crest line (for two-arm reefs: the other arm); crest cell z = 0.46 m MSL

reconstruction_check.what: volume of the reef grid read here (sum of max(reef - seabed, 0) over all finite reef cells, no thickness threshold, seabed from this script) against the volume stated by the model for the same version; a check that the surface was reconstructed as the viewer draws it
reconstruction_check.stated_source: model.js versions[lidar_2022].volume_m3 (both structures incl. toe berm and blanket)

secondary_structure.name: southern oval = shore-parallel breakwater (crest +1.50 mODN, NOT a surf reef)

crest_line.definition: cross-shore line through the highest cell of the secondary structure
